name: Equivocation
shortDef: Shifting between two meanings of the same word within one argument.
definition: Using a key word or phrase in one sense in one part of an argument and a different sense in another, so the conclusion seems to follow when it only follows because the word sounds the same.
howToSpot: Find the key word and ask what it means each time it appears.
Swap in a precise synonym each time: does the argument still work?
Watch technical words with everyday meanings, like 'significant' or 'theory'.
classicExample: The sign said 'fine for parking here,' so I figured parking there was fine.
legitimateVersion: Using a word with several meanings is fine when its sense stays fixed throughout, or when the speaker spells out which meaning applies and reasons from that one.

contrast.fal_straw_man: A straw man distorts someone else's position; equivocation shifts the meaning of a word inside the argument itself.
contrast.fal_false_analogy: A false analogy compares two things that differ in key ways; equivocation treats two meanings of one word as if they were the same.
